summary.text: Mark Pocan is the Democratic incumbent for Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District, which he has represented since 2013. A Kenosha native, he owned a printing business, served on the Dane County Board of Supervisors, and spent 14 years in the Wisconsin State Assembly. He serves on the House Appropriations and Foreign Affairs committees and is Chair Emeritus of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.

paragraphs.text: Pocan was born in Kenosha, Wisconsin, in 1964 (August 14, per Wikipedia), and was raised there, graduating from Mary D. Bradford High School in 1982.

He earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1986, then opened and owned Budget Signs & Specialties, a printing business. His House biography describes him as a former small business owner and union member.
Pocan served on the Dane County Board of Supervisors from 1991 to 1996.

He was elected to the Wisconsin State Assembly in 1998 to succeed Tammy Baldwin and served until 2013, sitting on the Joint Finance Committee for six years, including a term as co-chair, according to Wikipedia.
He was sworn in as U.S. Representative on January 3, 2013, succeeding Baldwin after she was elected to the U.S. Senate.

In the 119th Congress Pocan sits on the House Appropriations Committee (Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies; Financial Services and General Government subcommittees) and the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

He chaired the Congressional Progressive Caucus from 2017 to 2021 (alongside Pramila Jayapal), according to Wikipedia, and is now its Chair Emeritus. He co-chairs the Congressional Equality Caucus and co-founded and co-chairs the Labor Caucus and the Defense Spending Reduction Caucus.
